title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as companies pivot to meet new demands and the regulatory landscape shifts. Notable developments include a focus on satellite systems and innovative approaches to national security.

themes.title: Satellite Systems Surge
themes.body: Airbus is capitalizing on the increasing demand for satellite systems, a trend likely to continue as global connectivity needs rise. Meanwhile, the FCC's new licensing reforms could streamline satellite deployment, further fueling this growth.

themes.title: National Security Ventures
themes.body: Vast's new division for national security projects signals a growing recognition of the space domain's strategic importance. Similarly, Anduril and L3Harris's collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid highlights the competitive landscape for defense-related space initiatives.

themes.title: Regulatory Shifts Ahead
themes.body: The FCC's sweeping space reforms, including a new C-band auction, indicate a significant regulatory pivot that could reshape the satellite industry. This overhaul aims to enhance operational efficiency but may also invite new challenges for existing players.

themes.title: Funding and Innovation
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4B boost for space resilience underscores a commitment to strengthening national capabilities in this arena. Additionally, True Anomaly's recent $190M Series C round showcases the venture capital interest in space tech innovation.
